answer: A bounded-vouch quorum gives each established identity two signed endorsements per epoch, each backed by a per-identity bond and three vouches from disjoint trust sets. A fabricated identity costs its bond plus three scarce endorser slots, and a ring exhausts combined budgets after a small multiple of members, stranding new keys in a tundra of unvouched state while legitimate clusters form an oasis of verified quorum; no plume of shared history can supply independent endorsers.
